value.body: The Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI) monitors adverse drug reactions (ADRs) across the country. It is coordinated by the Indian Pharmacopoeia Commission (IPC), Ghaziabad, as the National Coordination Centre, with ADR Monitoring Centres (AMCs) mostly in medical colleges and hospitals. Staff collect, assess and report ADR cases and train health workers to report them.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Posts are advertised by IPC or by the institution hosting an AMC. Typical eligibility is a Pharm.D, an M.Pharm (often pharmacology or pharmacy practice) or a related degree, as stated in each advertisement. Selection is usually by written test and/or interview, often walk-in.

value.title: At a glance
items: Most posts are contractual and project-based, renewed periodically — not permanent government jobs.
Openings appear irregularly and are tied to individual centres.
Experience in case processing and causality assessment carries over to drug-safety roles in pharma companies and CROs.
